newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Tribunal to inquire into infection of blood supply.
newsitem.headline: Tribunal to inquire into infection of blood supply.

text.p: Health minister Michael Noonan announced details of the tribunal of inquiry being set up to investigate infection of the blood supply that was distributed for years by the Irish Blood Transfusion Services Board.
"It is being asked to address very difficult and sensitive issues, surrounding one of the worst public scandals which has arisen for many years," Noonan said on Thursday.
Most of the 1,600 or so people who have been found to have hepatitis C are women who were given the blood product Anti-D after a pregnancy.

One woman died recently, just before her compensation claim against the Blood Board and the Department of Health was to be heard by the High Court. The board has agreed to pay her family 175,000 punts compensation.
The former chief justice, Thomas Finlay, is to be the sole member of the tribunal.
In a novel move, a legal team is to be appointed to represent the public interest at that tribunal -- separate from the team that will represent the Blood Board and the Department of Health.
